entry.title: CSS: use {{CSSInfo}} for color-interpolation
entry.content:
Description

Replaces the hand-written formal-definition table on the color-interpolation page with {{CSSInfo}}, now that mdn-data has the property (mdn/data#1121, released in mdn-data 2.38.0).

Motivation

The hand-written table was wrong in two places:

  • Default value: it said auto. The SVG 2 definition gives sRGB, and so do Chromium (css_properties.json5), Gecko (longhands.toml) and WebKit (CSSProperties.json). WPT's svg/painting/inheritance.svg tests it. The page's own sRGB entry already says it's the default.
  • Applies to: it listed only <linearGradient> and <radialGradient>. The spec says container elements, graphics elements, gradient elements, <use> and <animate>.

{{CSSInfo}} also adds the rows the table didn't have, such as inherited, percentages and computed value.

Additional details

Built the page locally with rari 1.3.0, which pulled mdn-data 2.38.0. The rendered table shows initial value sRGB, applies to "Container elements, graphics elements, gradient elements, <use>, and <animate> in <svg>", inherited yes, computed value as specified, and animation type discrete.

Related issues and pull requests

  • mdn/data#1121 adds color-interpolation to mdn-data.

entry.title: ci(pr-check-lint_content): print linted merge + base-branch hint on failure
entry.content:
Description

Update the content lint workflow to print the linted merge commit and a hint to merge main when linting fails.

Motivation

Make it easier to understand lint failures caused by combining the PR with newer changes on main, which don't reproduce on the PR branch.

The workflow lints refs/pull/<n>/merge. In #45225, main had meanwhile gained its own named-feature() section, so the merge result contained a duplicate heading (MD024 on line 173) that didn't exist in the PR branch.

entry.title: Explain locked bodies in Request and Response clone()
entry.content:
Both clone() pages only mention a body that has already been used. Acquiring a body reader also makes cloning throw TypeError, even before the first read and while bodyUsed remains false.

Document the locked-body case and explain the getReader() trigger on both Request and Response. This follows Fetch's clone algorithms and its definition of an unusable body:
https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-request-clone
https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-response-clone

Checked in Node 24.22.0 for both interfaces: an unread locked body throws, releasing the unread reader lock allows cloning, and a consumed body still throws. Targeted Prettier and git diff --check pass. No browser or full content build run.

Updates cspell from 10.4.1 to 10.5.0

Release notes

Sourced from cspell's releases.

v10.5.0

Features

feat: Skip nested git worktrees by default (#9604)

Summary

cspell now skips git worktrees inside the root folder, such as .worktrees/feature or .claude/worktrees/feature. A worktree is another checkout of the same repository, often of another branch, so its files are not the files being checked.

A new preset in ignorePathPresets, nestedWorktrees, can disable this.

Fixes #9515

Feature

A repository with a worktree of its feature branch, made with git worktree add worktrees/feature feature:

project/
  README.md
  worktrees/
    feature/
      README.md

Before, running cspell in project/ checked both copies of README.md:

$ cspell .
README.md:3:21 - Unknown word (finshed) fix: (finished)
worktrees/feature/README.md:3:21 - Unknown word (finshed) fix: (finished)
CSpell: Files checked: 2, Issues found: 2 in 2 files.

After, it checks only the repository's own README.md:

$ cspell .
README.md:3:21 - Unknown word (finshed) fix: (finished)
CSpell: Files checked: 1, Issues found: 1 in 1 file.

Running cspell in worktrees/feature/ still checks that worktree.

To check nested worktrees again:

cspell.json

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from cspell's changelog.

  • 10.4.1: the locale is fr only. English words in the file are reported as unknown.
  • Now: the locales are fr,en again.

The fix for comment closers (#9496) and the fix for locales that aren't valid (#9501) still hold. Each of these gives en, or fr,en for the last one, because text after the locales that isn't a locale doesn't become one:

<!-- cspell:locale en -->
/* cspell:locale en*/
cspell:locale fr,en -- the rest

A directive's text runs to the end of the line. Before, the locale list was split only on spaces and commas, and the list was cut at the first piece that didn't look like a locale. A piece like en` failed that check, so the list stopped at fr.

Now the list ends at the first character that can't be part of a locale or a separator, such as a backtick or */, or at --, as in -->. The rest is then split into pieces, and the list still ends at the first piece that isn't a locale.

fix: Make [!…] in globs match characters that are not listed (#9622)

Summary

A [!…] bracket in a glob now matches any character that is not listed, as it does in git and shell globs. Before, e[!a].txt in .gitignore (with useGitignore) or ignorePaths matched ea.txt and e!.txt and skipped eb.txt, so cspell checked the files you meant to ignore and ignored the files you meant to check.

  • Applies to ignorePaths, .gitignore files read with useGitignore, files, and the filename globs in overrides.
  • [^…] already worked and is unchanged.

Fixes #9621

  • cspell-glob now asks picomatch to read globs in POSIX mode. The only change this makes is that [! starts a negated bracket, like [^.
  • Include mode gets the same fix, so [!a] means the same thing in files and in ignorePaths.

entry.title: Document Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only header
entry.content:
Summary

  • Add the reference page for the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only HTTP response header (files/en-us/web/http/reference/headers/cross-origin-opener-policy-report-only/index.md), wired to browser-compat: http.headers.Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only.
  • Document its directives (unsafe-none, same-origin, same-origin-allow-popups), the report-to parameter, disposition: "reporting" JSON report behavior, and note that noopener-allow-popups applies only to the enforced header per the WHATWG HTML Standard (Section 7.1.3).
  • Link Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only from Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and list it under Security on the HTTP headers reference overview page.
  • Add the coop entry under reporting server endpoints on Web/API/Reporting_API.

Motivation

Closes the missing reference documentation for Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only, whose browser compatibility data (http/headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only.json) is already present in mdn/browser-compat-data.

entry.title: Clarify that webRequest.HttpHeaders names can repeat
entry.content:
Description

Documents that header names in a webRequest.HttpHeaders array are not guaranteed to be unique, and how browsers differ in representing repeated headers:

  • Chrome keeps a separate entry for each occurrence of a header.
  • Firefox and Safari combine repeated headers into one entry, joining values with , (Firefox uses \n for Set-Cookie, WWW-Authenticate, and Proxy-Authenticate).

Motivation

The page didn't say whether name can repeat, which matters for anyone reading or modifying headers such as Set-Cookie.

Additional details

Browser behavior is based on the maintainer comment in #46472.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46472

entry.title: FF161 Cross-document view transitions: docs fixes
entry.content:
FF161 enables cross-document view transitions and render blocking in Nightly (https://bugzil.la/2084340).

This reviews the cross-document view transitions and render-blocking docs against the spec, WPT and BCD. Pretty much throwing Claude at it and then checking the validation makes sense.

View transitions:

  • @view-transition: the types descriptor is space-separated (<custom-ident>+, not #). Also fixed in the Using types guide.
  • @view-transition: push/replace navigations started by script also get a view transition; only navigations from the browser UI (address bar, bookmarks) are excluded
  • @view-transition: the types descriptor applies only to the document that contains the rule, so the types need to be declared in both documents
  • @view-transition: none and -ua- idents aren't valid types; none is the default for both descriptors; intro covers types; example duration (0.4s) and See also fixes
  • PageSwapEvent(), PageRevealEvent(): init and its members are optional and default to null; Return value; examples
  • PageSwapEvent.viewTransition: named the wrong interface
  • PageSwapEvent.activation: not null after a cross-origin redirect if the page is restored from the bfcache
  • PageRevealEvent: the bfcache example used pagehide instead of pageshow; moved into a Description
  • PageSwapEvent, PageRevealEvent, pageswap/pagereveal events: intros, inheritance, example headings and lead-ins, See also
  • CSSViewTransitionRule: APIRef group is View Transition API; the example logged the rule list, not the rule; navigation values

Render blocking:

  • HTMLLinkElement/HTMLScriptElement/HTMLStyleElement.blocking: "fetching of an external resource" was wrong for rel="expect" and <style>; say when rendering is blocked; script example used async on an inline script
  • <script>: said parser-inserted scripts don't block rendering; they do by default, and inline classic scripts never block
  • <link>, <style>: blocking attribute and notes; rel="expect" needs blocking="render"; <link> example now shows rel="expect"
  • rel: expect is an internal resource, not a link, identified by the href fragment
  • renderBlockingStatus: tautology in the intro, Value, Description, See also
  • Render blocking glossary: what blocks by default, and blocking on purpose

Related BCD: mdn/browser-compat-data#31150

Related docs work can be tracked in #46469
